verses.text: Now Joshua was old and well advanced in years. Yahweh said to him, “You are old and advanced in years, and there remains yet very much land to be possessed.
“This is the land that still remains: all the regions of the Philistines, and all the Geshurites;

from the Shihor, which is before Egypt, even to the border of Ekron northward, which is counted as Canaanite; the five lords of the Philistines; the Gazites, and the Ashdodites, the Ashkelonites, the Gittites, and the Ekronites; also the Avvim,
on the south; all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah that belongs to the Sidonians, to Aphek, to the border of the Amorites;
and the land of the Gebalites, and all Lebanon, toward the sunrise, from Baal Gad under Mount Hermon to the entrance of Hamath;

all the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephoth Maim, even all the Sidonians. I will drive them out from before the children of Israel. Just allocate it to Israel for an inheritance, as I have commanded you.
Now therefore divide this land for an inheritance to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.”
With him the Reubenites and the Gadites received their inheritance, which Moses gave them, beyond the Jordan eastward, even as Moses the servant of Yahweh gave them:
from Aroer, that is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and the city that is in the middle of the valley, and all the plain of Medeba to Dibon;
and all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, to the border of the children of Ammon;
and Gilead, and the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites, and all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan to Salecah;
all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and in Edrei (the same was left of the remnant of the Rephaim); for Moses attacked these, and drove them out.
Nevertheless the children of Israel didn’t drive out the Geshurites, nor the Maacathites: but Geshur and Maacath live within Israel to this day.
Only he gave no inheritance to the tribe of Levi. The offerings of Yahweh, the God of Israel, made by fire are his inheritance, as he spoke to him.
Moses gave to the tribe of the children of Reuben according to their families.
Their border was from Aroer, that is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and the city that is in the middle of the valley, and all the plain by Medeba;
Heshbon, and all its cities that are in the plain; Dibon, Bamoth Baal, Beth Baal Meon,
Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath,
Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth Shahar in the mount of the valley,
Beth Peor, the slopes of Pisgah, Beth Jeshimoth,

all the cities of the plain, and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, whom Moses struck with the chiefs of Midian, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the princes of Sihon, who lived in the land.
The children of Israel also killed Balaam the son of Beor, the soothsayer, with the sword, among the rest of their slain.
The border of the children of Reuben was the bank of the Jordan. This was the inheritance of the children of Reuben according to their families, the cities and its villages.
Moses gave to the tribe of Gad, to the children of Gad, according to their families.
Their border was Jazer, and all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the children of Ammon, to Aroer that is near Rabbah;
and from Heshbon to Ramath Mizpeh, and Betonim; and from Mahanaim to the border of Debir;

and in the valley, Beth Haram, Beth Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, the Jordan’s bank, to the uttermost part of the sea of Chinnereth beyond the Jordan eastward.
This is the inheritance of the children of Gad according to their families, the cities and its villages.
Moses gave an inheritance to the half-tribe of Manasseh. It was for the half-tribe of the children of Manasseh according to their families.
Their border was from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the villages of Jair, which are in Bashan, sixty cities.

Half Gilead, Ashtaroth, and Edrei, the cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, were for the children of Machir the son of Manasseh, even for the half of the children of Machir according to their families.
These are the inheritances which Moses distributed in the plains of Moab, beyond the Jordan at Jericho, eastward.
But Moses gave no inheritance to the tribe of Levi. Yahweh, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, as he spoke to them.

footnotes.content: Joshua is old, and the Lord reminds him there is still much work to be done. How often do we think our years of useful service are behind us? But God's work spans seasons—what we do now may be handing the torch to the next generation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Philistines and Geshurites still held their land. Unfinished work marks the edge of faith—the conquest was real and glorious, yet the promise called Israel to live faithfully *in the midst* of neighbors who had not yet yielded to the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Gazites, Ashdodites, Ashkelonites, Gittites, Ekronites—each people had their own gods and ways. The Lord names them clearly: He sees every nation, and His patience with them mirrors His patience in drawing us too.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The southern land of the Canaanites remained. Maps and boundaries matter to the Lord—He is precise in His promises and calls us to account for what He has given us to steward.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From Baal Gad under Mount Hermon to Hamath—a vast stretch of land *toward the sunrise*. That direction matters: east, where the morning comes. The Lord's gifts often come with a call to move forward, into the light.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "I will drive them out from before the children of Israel." The work is God's first; the allocation and stewardship are Israel's. We too are promised the victory that matters—and called to walk faithfully in what He gives.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua is told to divide the land among nine and a half tribes. Leadership often means stepping back and giving others their inheritance. This is an act of faith and trust in God's provision for the whole people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Reuben and Gad received their inheritance as Moses had already given it. This continuity matters—what one faithful leader began, the next one honors and completes. Generations serve together in the Lord's purpose.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Aroer, Arnon, Medeba—real places where real people lived. The Lord knows every valley and city; He knows the ground we stand on. Our lives are not abstractions to Him but woven into the fabric of His history.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sihon the Amorite king once held this land and reigned in Heshbon. The Lord removed what opposed His people so that they could inherit. His protection is as real as His promises.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Gilead, Geshur, Maacath, Mount Hermon, Bashan—a catalogue of geography that belonged to promise. The specific naming tells us: nothing in God's plan is vague or uncared-for. Every place holds His attention.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Og of Bashan was a Rephaim, a giant. Moses defeated him. The record reminds us: the Lord has already done mighty things on behalf of His people. Our inheritance rests on victories already won.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Israel did not drive out the Geshurites and Maacathites; they lived *within* Israel to that day. Not every enemy is removed; some remain as a test of faith. How we live alongside difficulty shapes our character.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Levi received no land inheritance—the Lord Himself was their portion. How radical: a tribe whose wealth was not measured in acres but in belonging to God. That promise still stands for those who serve Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses gave to Reuben according to their families. Each family, each household, mattered in the distribution. The Lord sees us not as a mass but as beloved, particular people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The border was from Aroer, the valley of Arnon, the plain of Medeba. Borders mark where one family's responsibility begins. To know our boundaries is to know where the Lord calls us to be faithful.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Heshbon, Dibon, Bamoth Baal, Beth Baal Meon—city by city, the inheritance took shape. Kingdom work is never abstract; it is built in real places, among real neighbors, one family at a time.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath were given to Reuben. These names held no power in themselves, yet each carried the meaning of home, security, a place to raise children in the Lord's promise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth Shahar—the catalogue continues. Every city listed belonged to someone's family story. The Lord's distribution is thorough, and His care extends to the smallest household.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Beth Peor overlooks the slopes of Pisgah where Moses died looking at the land he could not enter. Now his people inherited what he could only see from afar. His faith was not disappointed, though by different means than he imagined.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sihon and the Midianite princes—Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, Reba—were defeated by Moses. This chapter honors the victories God won through Moses, anchoring Reuben's inheritance in His faithfulness across generations.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Balaam the soothsayer was killed among the slain. He had sought to curse Israel, but his curse turned to blessing. The Lord's victory is complete—even those who oppose His people find judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Jordan's bank was Reuben's border. A river marks security; you can see who approaches. Boundaries are gifts of peace and watchfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now the tribe of Gad receives their inheritance. Each tribe mattered; each had their share in the Lord's promise. No one was forgotten.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jazer, Gilead, half the land of Ammon—Gad's border extended to the settlements of their neighbors. Living near others tests our faith and calls us to faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Heshbon to Ramath Mizpeh, Betonim to Debir—the boundaries of Gad were clearly marked. When we know where we are called to serve, we can give ourselves fully.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Beth Haram, Beth Nimrah, Succoth, Zaphon—and the Jordan's bank marked the eastern edge of the kingdom of Sihon, now Gad's inheritance. The Sea of Chinnereth (Galilee) glimmers beyond. Each boundary honors the Lord's sovereignty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Gad's inheritance was complete—cities and villages, all accounted for. The Lord's work is not left undone; every family has their place.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Half of Manasseh received their inheritance. Half the tribe had already settled in Canaan; now their brothers across the Jordan had their portion too. The Lord's promises extend to all His people, wherever they dwell.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mahanaim, Bashan, sixty cities of Jair—Manasseh's inheritance was rich and vast. Numbers often show God's generosity: sixty cities are not meant to be stingy. His hand is always open.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Half Gilead, Ashtaroth, Edrei—the inheritance of the sons of Machir. Even within a tribe, families were honored and named. The Lord knows us by name and gives us our place.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses distributed these inheritances in the plains of Moab, beyond the Jordan at Jericho. One faithful leader handed the torch to another; what was promised came to pass across generations.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this verse: to serve the Lord is to receive Him as your portion, richer than any land. When we give ourselves to His work, we inherit not acres but His presence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
